meaning: Sets the VA shunt valve resistance in Model_6 to 1.4e6, the same value as Model_1, so a fixed one-way drain from CSF to central vein whenever ICP exceeds Pcv. Because ResistorValve has no opening pressure, this number alone sets how fast CSF leaves once the gradient is positive.

could_move.what: Shunt flow and CSF volume in any m3/m6 run with shunt = :va; the comment at Params.jl:138 records a case where CSF dural volume went negative while pressures looked settled, so this value can push volumes out of physical range
M1-vs-M3 shunt comparisons lose their like-for-like framing if this diverges from the Model_1 value
Shunt-element equations that consume the parameter
Posture-related decks, since the VA drainage gradient depends on Pcv and thus on posture

expectation: Lower Rva_shunt_v means more drainage, lower ICP and faster CSF volume loss; higher means less. Whether 1.4e6 keeps CSF dural volume non-negative in Model_6 is not something I can tell from the context.

check.why: Runs a single verification solve rather than a re-fit; inspect CSF dural volume and shunt flow for negative or drifting values.
